neighbours.label: the determiner that opens a complement clause after a first-person or reported opinion verb ('complains that the ...', 'I find that the ...'); the same nouns in plain declarative sentences stay quiet
fire: My neighbor complains that the bins are never emptied on time.
Honestly, I find that the second season drags a little in the middle.
Notice that the handle on this pan stays cool while cooking.
Tom keeps saying that the new office is far too cold.
I feel that the ending of the book was a little rushed.
Some readers complained that the font in the paperback is tiny.
I noticed that the cheaper brand actually lasts longer.
My sister insists that the old recipe tastes better.
quiet: Our street has bins that are emptied every Thursday morning.
The second season has ten episodes and a long finale.
This pan has a long handle and a heavy base.
Tom works in the new office on the fourth floor.
The book has twelve chapters and a short epilogue.
The paperback edition costs eight dollars at most stores.
The cheaper brand comes in three sizes and two colors.
My sister bakes bread from an old family recipe.

predictions: fire 0.25-0.5 on ' the'/' this' right after 'that' following find/complain/notice; neutral declaratives below 0.1
notes: Card: ' the' x9, ' this' x3, mostly after 'that' in chatty first-person text ('Mary complains that the', 'Notice that the', 'I find that the', 'downloading files from the').
